instruction: Change the GIMP theme to Gray.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened GIMP, navigated to Edit > Preferences > Theme, observed available themes (Dark, Gray, Light, System), checked Icon Theme section, tried web search for Blue theme, and correctly declared the task infeasible since no Blue theme exists.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can launch GIMP from app launcher, navigate Edit > Preferences, browse Theme and Icon Theme sections, read available theme options, recognize infeasible tasks
metadata.task_rationale: Since the agent demonstrated ability to navigate GIMP Preferences > Theme and read available themes, this variation asks it to actually select an existing theme (Gray) instead of a non-existent one.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing GIMP theme to Gray via Edit > Preferences > Theme. Evaluator reads gimprc config file and uses check_config_status to verify the theme key has value '"Gray"' (quoted, matching gimprc format). [Fixed: changed rules format from {expected:{theme:Gray}} to {key:theme,value:'"Gray"'} to match check_config_status parameter signature].
fix_history: Fix 1: Changed evaluator.expected.rules from {expected:{theme:Gray}} to {key:theme,value:'"Gray"'} to match check_config_status which accesses rule['key'] and rule['value']. Added escaped quotes around Gray to match gimprc format (theme "Gray").

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (gimp_config_file) correctly reads gimprc from ~/.config/GIMP/2.10/gimprc, which is the right file to check GIMP theme settings.
Expected rules format {"key": "theme", "value": "\"Gray\""} correctly matches check_config_status parameter signature, which accesses rule["key"] and rule["value"] (gimp.py:531-532).

The gimprc line '(theme "Gray")' after parsing (strip, lstrip '(', rstrip ')', split) produces items=['theme', '"Gray"']. items[0]=='theme' matches rule["key"] and items[-1]=='"Gray"' matches rule["value"] with escaped quotes.
Single instruction requirement (change theme to Gray) is fully covered by the evaluator. No missing verification steps.
